---
title: "Scaling Machine Learning Systems"
subtitle: "Semester plan · Volume II"
---

## Overview {#overview}

This course studies distributed training, communication, fault recovery, and inference across clusters. Students
need the introductory course or equivalent machine learning systems knowledge. The supporting textbook is
[MLSysBook Volume II](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/).

## Syllabus and schedule {#syllabus}

The adaptable [semester syllabus](https://mlsysbook.ai/instructors/scale-syllabus.html)
contains the course overview, prerequisites, weekly schedule, and teaching notes.
The weekly plan pairs textbook readings with systems labs and decision logs. A capstone asks students to defend a distributed system design using workloads, measurements, and analytical models.

The syllabus remains the source for the teaching sequence. An institutional
offering should specify its own dates, submission deadlines, and local policies.

## Materials {#materials}

| Resource | Use |
|:---|:---|
| [Volume II](https://mlsysbook.ai/vol2/) | The weekly readings. |
| [Lecture slides](https://mlsysbook.ai/slides/vol2.html) | One deck per chapter, with speaker notes and in-class exercises. |
| [Interactive labs](https://mlsysbook.ai/labs/) | Browser-based systems experiments that pair with the readings. |

## For instructors {#for-instructors}

The [Instructor Hub](https://mlsysbook.ai/instructors/) provides
[pedagogy](https://mlsysbook.ai/instructors/pedagogy.html),
[assessment](https://mlsysbook.ai/instructors/assessment.html),
[TA preparation](https://mlsysbook.ai/instructors/ta-guide.html), and
[customization guidance](https://mlsysbook.ai/instructors/customization.html).
This course can also run as the second half of a two-semester sequence after the
[introductory course](../intro/index.qmd); the
[course map](https://mlsysbook.ai/instructors/course-map.html) shows how they connect.

## Offerings {#offerings}

The [course directory](../index.qmd) lists courses at other
institutions that use MLSysBook. Each institution maintains its own syllabus,
schedule, and enrollment information.
